text: Apply within 48 hours of a job posting going live — most ATS systems rank early applicants higher.
Tailor your resume keywords to match the job description exactly — ATS filters reject near-matches.
Track every application in a spreadsheet with dates and follow-up reminders — silence after 10 days means it's time to nudge.
Target companies that posted the same role multiple times in 90 days — it signals high hiring volume and less competition per opening.
Referrals get interviewed 5-10x more often than cold applications — spend as much time networking as applying.
Quantify every bullet point with a number — impact, scale, or percentage improvement.
Lead each bullet with a strong action verb, not 'responsible for' or 'worked on'.
Keep it to one page unless you have 8+ years of experience — recruiters spend under 10 seconds on a first pass.
Cut objective statements entirely — replace with a 2-line summary that states your niche and biggest win.
List projects with a live link or repo — recruiters trust what they can click through more than what they read.
Prepare 3 STAR stories that can flex to answer 'leadership', 'conflict', and 'failure' questions interchangeably.
Ask about the team's current biggest challenge — it shows genuine interest and gives you real signal on the role.
Practice explaining your resume projects out loud in under 90 seconds each — rambling is the top reason strong candidates lose momentum.
Research the interviewer on LinkedIn beforehand — a shared background gives you an easy, genuine icebreaker.
Never give a number first in salary negotiation — ask for the budgeted range before revealing your expectation.
